_readme: The living source registry (owner directive, 2026-08-09): every source this loop uses to DISCOVER new listings, ENRICH existing ones, and MAINTAIN them (detect closures, moves, schedule changes). docs/source-registry.md is the human half — read it before adding or dropping a source. Every source carries lastVerified (the day it was last actually exercised from this environment) and status as observed THAT day, because reachability here is a fact about the egress proxy as much as about the source. Update lastVerified whenever a source is exercised; a source not exercised for 14+ days is stale and its status is a claim, not a fact.

sources.name: NYC Open Data (Socrata)
sources.cadence: daily delta check via dataUpdatedAt on tracked datasets

datasets.9nt8-h7nd: NTA 2020 neighborhood POLYGONS (GeoJSON) — real boundaries; replaces Nominatim bounding boxes everywhere
datasets.w3wp-dpdi: NYC Parks Public Events, next 14 days — MAINTENANCE signal: program activity per park

sources.notes: The catalog API (api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1?domains=data.cityofnewyork.us) is itself queryable — search it before assuming a dataset does not exist.

sources.name: NYC Parks pages (recreationcenters, parks, per-facility)
sources.cadence: weekly re-fetch of the rec-center directory; its closure/alert banners are the maintenance signal (Brownsville pool closed, J. Hood Wright summer closure — both caught from banners)
sources.notes: Parse the MARKUP not the flattened text; read the LABELLED phone, never the first 10-digit number (fax sits beside it on 4 of 9 pages).

sources.name: SerpAPI — structured Google Maps results (owner-provided key, 2026-08-09)
sources.access: curl via src/scripts/serp.py; key in .env.local (SERPAPI_API_KEY, gitignored). Free plan: 250 searches/month, HARD cap
sources.cadence: ~2 calls per neighbourhood round; 25-call reserve enforced in serp.py for maintenance emergencies; ledger at scratchpad serp_ledger.json
sources.notes: One call returns up to 20 places with name, FULL address, phone, type, gps, place_id, rating, hours, and 'Permanently closed' markers (the maintenance signal). First two calls found New Generation School of Martial Arts (395 Maple St, 11225 — a PLG venue NO other tier had) and a FOURTH operator at Major Owens (Globall Sports Centers). Noise profile: results can include out-of-market places (a Sterling VA gym appeared in a Brooklyn-centred search) — the entity and geo checks stay mandatory. Never spend a search on what a free tier answers.

sources.name: Yelp Fusion API (owner-provided key, 2026-08-09)
sources.access: curl via src/scripts/yelp.py; key in .env.local (YELP_API_KEY, gitignored). Free tier: 5,000 calls/day
sources.cadence: discovery per neighbourhood round; WEEKLY closure sweep of the whole live pool by phone-join (the pool's normalized phone digits are Yelp's join key; ~1,100 calls, well inside one day's budget)
sources.notes: Structured name/address/phone/categories/coordinates plus is_closed — the closure signal nothing else on this registry has, maintained by Yelp. First PLG radius call added Rebel Fitness Bar (1196 Nostrand, 11225), TNK-Jujitsu, All Sports For All People (883 Classon, 11225) and a second Maple St dojo. Noise profile: pads thin radii with out-of-area results (a Bronx instructor and a Long Beach gym inside a 1.2km PLG search) and lists home-based instructors with no venue — row() flags missing street addresses, and the no-fixed-venue prohibition plus the operator-site check stay mandatory. is_closed=True is a LEAD for the closure check, never an automatic quarantine.

sources.name: Owner-supplied verified provider spreadsheets
sources.access: uploaded .xlsx; parsed and cross-checked against the pool, saved as src/scripts/ownerVerifiedQueue.json
sources.notes: Two received so far (STRICT_REBUILD; NEXT_20, 2026-08-09 — 9 of its 20 not yet in the pool). Highest-trust discovery tier but still verified per candidate before create: the first spreadsheet contained 7 venues that already had live records, and acting on it unchecked would have created duplicates.

sources.name: Search-index mining over walled directories (Yelp, Sawyer, ClassPass, Mindbody)
sources.access: agent WebSearch tool with allowed_domains — NOT curl, NOT a browser; both are blocked (Yelp/Sawyer bot-wall curl; Chromium cannot CONNECT through the egress proxy at all, verified 2026-08-09 against example.com)
sources.cadence: per-neighbourhood rounds; re-run a neighbourhood's query set when it is next worked
sources.notes: Yelp titles carry 'NAME - ADDRESS - phone'; Sawyer titles carry 'NAME - ADDRESS - NEIGHBORHOOD'. The index IS the dataset. Query templates in docs/source-registry.md. Everything found is a LEAD: entity check against the operator's own site stays mandatory.

sources.name: Operators' own sites (locations pages, schedules, contact pages)
sources.cadence: re-fetch every listing's website on a rolling ~30-day cycle; diffs in address/phone/schedule blocks are the maintenance signal
sources.notes: THE source of truth for every field on a listing. Its location finder beats every search summary (rule already in CLAUDE.md). A 404 on a guessed slug is not evidence of closure; a farewell message or a removed location IS.

sources.name: Franchise / chain / network location directories
sources.access: curl; one request returns every branch with address+phone
sources.cadence: monthly re-fetch per chain; a branch disappearing from its own chain's list is the strongest closure signal there is
sources.examples: ymcanyc.org/locations (24 branches, one request), championstkd.com (60+ NYC-area schools), goldfishswimschool.com, britishswimschool.com, codeninjas.com, sheridanfencing.com, advantagetennisclubs.com, thecliffsclimbing.com, vitalclimbinggym.com
sources.notes: Root-domain cards are defect predictors, per-location paths are canonical (already in CLAUDE.md). Maintain a chains list; every new multi-site operator found joins it.

sources.name: Shared-venue tenant expansion (one building, several operators)
sources.access: the venue's own site names its operators; then each operator's site
sources.cadence: whenever a multi-tenant venue is touched
sources.notes: Major Owens Center, 1561 Bedford Ave 11225: New Heights (basketball) + Imagine Swimming (pool) + Asphalt Green (turf field) all run children's programs inside one building the OSM sweep counted as ONE venue. Rec centers, armories, JCCs/Ys and piers all have this shape. One venue can be worth 3-4 listings under the rented-venue rule (continuing program at a fixed address).

sources.name: NYC parenting directories (Mommy Poppins, Macaroni KID, Brooklyn Bridge Parents, New York Family)
sources.access: articles/guides curl-reachable; Mommy Poppins directory listings render client-side, reach them via index-mining instead
sources.cadence: seasonal — camp guides land Jan-Apr, class roundups Aug-Sep
sources.notes: DISCOVERY SOURCE, not a card host (letsgobaby directive). Their per-neighbourhood camp guides name operators with addresses. Date-check every article: a 2018 roundup lists closed businesses.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap via Overpass
sources.notes: DEMOTED from primary to one voice among several (2026-08-09): its PLG sweep returned 3 venues in a neighbourhood the index tier shows has ~10. It sees mapped storefronts, misses second-floor studios, church-basement programs and shared-venue tenants entirely. Its addresses can be stale (BKLA had moved) or wrong (Sportspark's number). Still worth running — it finds mapped venues other tiers miss — but its count is NEVER a neighbourhood ceiling.

sources.name: Nominatim geocoding
sources.notes: Street-grade only (place_rank >= 26); borough bounding-box guard mandatory — it resolved three numbered-avenue Manhattan addresses to Westchester.

sources.name: NYS DOH children's camp permits
sources.access: no downloadable dataset found (2026-08-09); health.ny.gov pages describe the permit regime only
sources.cadence: re-check quarterly for a published dataset
sources.notes: Every legal NYC day camp holds a DOHMH permit — the permit roll would be a camp CENSUS. Worth an owner-side ask (311/FOIL or DOHMH ABCEats-style portal) — highest-value single acquisition on this list.

sources.name: Yelp Fusion API / Google Places API
sources.access: requires API keys the project does not hold
sources.notes: Both halves now supplied: SerpAPI (serpapi-google-maps) and Yelp Fusion (yelp-fusion). Entry kept for history.

sources.name: Playwright/Chromium scraping
sources.access: BLOCKED in this environment — Chromium cannot CONNECT through the egress proxy (ERR_CONNECTION_RESET on every site incl. example.com, with proxy configured and CA trusted; verified 2026-08-09)
sources.notes: Recorded so nobody spends an afternoon rediscovering this. Index-mining substitutes for the walled-directory tier.
